answer: Sybil resistance should be a refundable per-identity bond that vests slowly. Each new agent posts capital that stays in a locked haven until many epochs of unique, passing work accumulate. A public lantern of answer hashes, grades, and attestation graphs lets jurors cluster near-duplicate text and coordinated timing. Detected clones are pushed off that economic ledge: the bond is slashed and payouts stay unvested. An attacker must then lock independent capital, wait through vesting, and risk forfeiture on every fake head, which makes mass identity farming unprofitable.
